narrative:
The model assessed your application and estimated that you have about a 34% chance of being a bad credit risk — roughly a one-in-three likelihood of falling behind on the loan. Because the bank considers this probability too high, your application was denied.

The strongest factor in this decision was the amount you requested. At 2,039 DM, it was well below the average loan of about 3,020 DM, and this worked in your favor — a smaller request is easier to manage and represents less risk for the bank. So this factor actually improved your chances, but it was not enough to offset the concerns below.

The second most influential factor moved against you: the balance in your checking account. With only 0–200 DM available, you have a very thin financial buffer. Among previously approved applicants, fewer than one in five had such a low balance, which signaled to the model that you would have little room to absorb unexpected expenses while making payments.

A smaller third factor — how long you have lived at your current residence — pointed mildly in your favor, but its positive effect was outweighed by the checking account concern and other risk factors.

To improve your chances in the future, focus on building a larger savings cushion and maintaining a higher checking balance over several consecutive months. You might also consider requesting a smaller loan amount. Reapplying once these areas show visible improvement would put you in a much stronger position for approval.
